answer: A stake-bonded identity vault makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can transact, and proven misbehavior slashes the bond. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand deposits, while honest agents get theirs back. Like an umber gate guarding a garden, the bond lets genuine participants in and prices out anyone trying to flood the network with cheap clones.
